subject.title: fix(agents): cloud thinking models time out at 120s during reasoning (#80349) [AI-assisted]

question: After the call-site guard bug and proof gap are fixed, should thinking-enabled cloud runs disable the implicit 120s idle watchdog by default?
rationale: The code change intentionally trades a false 120s timeout for a longer silent-run window, and that default-timeout policy affects existing cloud thinking users beyond unit-test correctness.

options.title: Accept after guard repair and live proof
options.body: Land the narrow thinking-aware exemption once the runner passes id/provider metadata and redacted live Gemini proof shows the reported timeout is gone.

options.title: Require explicit timeout configuration
options.body: Keep the implicit cloud watchdog unchanged and ask users to raise models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds for slow thinking models.

options.title: Pause for a broader timeout design
options.body: Hold this PR behind the broader generation-timeout configuration work if maintainers want a single policy for silent thinking and runaway generation.

recommendation.title: Accept after guard repair and live proof
recommendation.body: Land the narrow thinking-aware exemption once the runner passes id/provider metadata and redacted live Gemini proof shows the reported timeout is gone.

likelyOwner.reason: This login is tied to the original idle-timeout behavior and is the strongest code-history owner for the timeout policy choice.
